combat_history.event: Deployed to the Tibetan plateau during the China–India border standoff.
combat_history.significance: Put mobile armour where heavy MBTs struggle at altitude.

modernization.description: Continued PLA fielding and export marketing of the VT5 variant.
modernization.impact: Spreads a capable light tank to specific theatres and buyers.

vulnerabilities.description: Light weight means less armour than an MBT.
vulnerabilities.context: More vulnerable to heavy anti-tank fire.

vulnerabilities.description: The 105 mm is less potent than the 125 mm on heavy tanks against modern MBTs.
vulnerabilities.context: Designed for terrain access, not tank duels.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Mobile armoured support in high-altitude, riverine and amphibious terrain.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Light combined-arms brigades; rapid-reaction and plateau forces.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Type 99A is a 55t MBT for plains; the Type 15 trades protection/firepower for altitude and terrain access.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: China's heavy and light tanks — different jobs.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Heavy MBTs the Type 15 is not meant to slug it out with head-on.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Why China fields a light tank at altitude.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The U.S. Army's new light protected-firepower vehicle addresses a similar need for deployable armour.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The return of the light tank.

doctrine.role: Light tank providing mobile armoured firepower where heavy MBTs cannot easily operate.
doctrine.employment: Plateau, riverine and amphibious manoeuvre with a 105 mm gun and strong mobility.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Tailor armour to terrain — accept lighter protection for altitude and soft-ground access.
doctrine.threat_context: Deployed on the Tibetan plateau against India and relevant to southern amphibious operations.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the heavy Type 99A and the wider revival of light tanks (M10 Booker).
